title: Editorial long-form article
description: A reading page for essays, reports, and case studies: one centered text column held to a 60-72ch measure, a strong headline block with standfirst and byline, pull quotes and figures that break out wider than the text column, and footnotes or sidenotes that never interrupt the line of reading.
intent: Make long text comfortable to read start to finish and give figures and quotes room without breaking the reading rhythm.
characteristics: named grid lines for text, wide, and full-bleed figures
headline block: kicker, title, standfirst, byline, date
pull quotes set larger in the display face, never repeated body text
sidenotes in the margin at wide widths, inline footnotes on narrow
interaction: Mostly static. Optional reading-progress indicator and in-page anchors for headings; footnote references jump to the note and back.
responsive: Grid collapses to one column with side padding at narrow widths; wide figures become full width; sidenotes turn into numbered notes after the paragraph.
accessibility: One h1 and an ordered heading outline; body text at least 16px with 1.5+ line height; figures use figure/figcaption; footnote links have back-links with accessible names; images have alt text written for the argument they support.
limitations: Wrong for scannable reference docs; use the docs layout instead.
Sidenotes need enough viewport width; plan the narrow fallback first.
Depends on real long-form content; placeholder text hides measure and rhythm problems.
